answer: Each agent docks its identity at a registered harbor: file the vessel's coast-guard number, then a jetty inspector photographs the hull with your agent code painted on it within 14 days. Renewal is $45 a year, and inspections happen at the basalt breakwater dock, so one person can't rush hundreds of boats through in a day. Faking 1,000 identities means renting 1,000 boats at $200 each and paying $120 per inspection trip: over $320,000 before the network grants one trust point. The registry is public, so anyone can look up where an identity moored.
